questions.stem: A patient was put on morphine for cancer pain due to carcinoma of the pancreas. His pain got relieved initially, but now, after 3 weeks, the pain is not get relieved. The reason is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Desensitization of opioid receptors
  • Chronic use of opioids leads to the development of tolerance.
  • To get the same effect, we need to use a high drug dose.
  • This is due to the desensitization of opioid receptors
  • Tolerance develops to all the effects of morphine except Miosis, Constipation, and Convulsions.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 381

questions.stem: Placebo works by releasing endorphins, which are endogenous opioids. These endorphins mainly act at:
questions.solutionHtml:
Mu receptor

The mu receptors are a class of receptors that neuromodulate different physiological functions, but above all, nociception but also stress, temperature, respiration, endocrine activity, gastrointestinal activity, memory, mood, and motivation because these receptors bind opioids and are called mu-opioid receptors (MORs).



Lange Katzung, Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 554

questions.stem: An Intern gave a trauma patient with a head injury morphine to relieve a headache. But the senior resident told to intern that he shouldn’t have administered it. The reason is?

options.label: B
options.text: Opioids also can cause marked respiratory depression

options.label: C
options.text: Morphine interferes with the assessment of progress in head injury cases

questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • As opioids induce retention of CO2, it increases intracranial tension, worsening the head injury.
  • Therapeutic doses of opioids also can cause marked respiratory depression in these patients.
  • Clinical manifestations like vomiting, miosis, and altered sensorium produced by morphine interfere with assessing progress in head injury cases.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 502

questions.stem: A patient was put on morphine for cancer pain due to carcinoma of the pancreas. His pain was relieved, and the patient took around 6 doses of morphine to get rid of the pain. He came to the emergency room with pinpoint pupil and respiratory depression. The best drug to reverse this is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Naloxone

 Naloxone  is an opioid antagonist. It is used in the treatment of opioid toxicity. It counters and blocks the unwanted effects of opioid overdose.

questions.stem: An opioid addict was bought to the psychiatry Department for de-addiction. The drug used for opioid dependence is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Methadone

The maintenance Drug for Dependence on Opioids Is Methadone.

  • Methadone is long-acting, prevents withdrawal effects during opioid deaddiction, and also decreases the euphoric effect(kick) of opioids.
  • Methadone is a potent mu-receptor agonist, and it suppresses the symptoms of opioids.
  • Withdrawal
  • Tolerance and physical dependence occur only at a slow rate with methadone compared to morphine.
  • It is administered once daily, as it is long-acting.
  • On abrupt discontinuation, it produces only mild withdrawal signs and symptoms.
  • Hence methadone is used as substitution therapy for opioid dependence.
  • A drug to prevent relapse of addiction is naltrexone.
  • Naltrexone blocks all opioid receptors.
  • When the patient tries to retake opioids, he will not get a euphoric effect as all the receptors are already blocked by naltrexone. So without getting a euphoric effect, the patient will not be retaking opioids.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 504
